line: Crowley on Swords: Air, the Ace of Swords as the Essence of the Vau, the Princes, and the letter of Air (pdf p23, p24, p46, p139, p210).

sections.title: Air
sections.line: Crowley's attribution of Swords to Air (pdf p24) and his statements on Air and the Wind (pdf p210).

quotes.quote: “Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;
Air is the result of the conjunction of Fire and Water
In nature, the obvious symbol of Air is the Wind

sections.title: The Vau of the Ace
sections.line: Crowley on the Ace of Swords as the Essence of the Vau of Tetragrammaton (pdf p210) and on the Princes as the Forces of the letter Vau (pdf p139).

quotes.quote: The Ace of Swords is the primordial Energy of Air, the Essence of the Vau of Tetragrammaton
The Princes represent the Forces of the letter Vau in the Name.

sections.title: The letter of Air
sections.line: Crowley on the letters Shin, Mem and Aleph for the elements (pdf p23) and on the letter Aleph in the card of the Fool (pdf p46).

quotes.quote: These elements are represented in the Hebrew alphabet by the letters Shin, Mem and Aleph.
This card is attributed to the letter Aleph, which means an Ox, but by its shape the Hebrew letter (so it is said) represents a plough‐ share; thus the significance is primarily Phallic.
